prs.title: fix(spy): use primordials to allow spying on builtins
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11827

Mocks called builtin methods directly, so spying on them recursed (`WeakMap.prototype.set`, `Array.prototype.push`, `Function.prototype.apply`), looped in `vi.clearAllMocks()` (`Set.prototype.delete`) or recorded internal calls (`FinalizationRegistry.prototype.register`, `Object.defineProperty`). The originals are now stored in `primordials.ts` with Node.js primordial names.

`Promise` is still read at call time because zone.js replaces it.

prs.title: fix(browser): scale the iframe for preview without the UI
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body: With `browser.ui: false`, the orchestrator asks the provider to resize the page through `__vitest_viewport` (since #9745). The preview provider has no such command, so the run failed with `Provider preview does not support command "__vitest_viewport"`. Preview cannot resize the user's window, so the iframe is now scaled to fit the page, as in UI mode.

prs.title: fix: avoid leaking the context expect
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11839

With `isolate: false`, a test that reads `expect` from its context kept its whole file and fixture values alive. `createExpect` added the built-in matchers again to each local `expect`, and `chai.use()` keeps every plugin closure.

- add `customMatchers` and `benchMatchers` only to the global `expect`
- call the `expect.extend` plugin directly instead of with `chai.use()`; this also releases the matchers that setup files add for each test file

prs.title: fix(browser): fix expect.element with `message` and remove redundant `[ERROR]` in trace steps
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11753

Previously, browser mode ignored the `message` option of `expect.element` in trace step names, while Node's `expect.poll` steps include it. Browser steps also added `[ERROR]` to the name of a failed step, although the entry already records its status.

This PR includes the message in browser trace step names and drops `[ERROR]` from them. For example,

```ts
await expect.element(page.getByRole('heading'), { message: 'heading shown' }).toHaveTextContent('Welcome')
```

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| without `message` | `toHaveTextContent` | `toHaveTextContent` |
| with `message` | `toHaveTextContent` | `heading shown (toHaveTextContent)` |
| failed | `toHaveTextContent [ERROR]` | `toHaveTextContent` |

Playwright trace event is label only without status semantics, so they still keep `[ERROR]` on failure.

prs.title: fix(coverage): transform untested files with correct project
prs.author: AriPerkkio

prs.title: fix(experimental): skip ambiguous `expect.poll` trace steps in concurrent tests
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11753

Previously, `experimental.traceTimeline` could misattribute steps from the global `expect.poll` to the wrong failing test when tests ran with `test.concurrent`.

This PR skips `expect.poll` steps from the global `expect` by guarding them with the condition `getRunningTests().size === 1`.

prs.title: fix: report fixture teardown errors once
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
`callFixtureCleanupFrom` kept a cleanup in the list when it threw, so `callFixtureCleanup` awaited the same rejected teardown again and the error was reported twice (since #9450). The loop also stopped at the first error, so the other teardowns (including the fixture's dependencies) never ran, and with `retry` the next attempt failed on the previous attempt's teardown error.

Cleanups are now removed from the list before they run, every cleanup runs even if one throws, and several errors are thrown as an `AggregateError`.

prs.title: fix: improve diffs for asymmetric matchers
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #5714
Fixes #8913
Fixes #11854

- `objectContaining` diffs show the keys the matcher does not check as unchanged lines, also at the top level.
- `arrayContaining` diffs keep the received order and show missing items as removed lines.
- Only non-negated `objectContaining`/`arrayContaining` are unwrapped; `expect.extend` matchers, `schemaMatching` and negated matchers are printed as is.
- `toHaveBeenCalledWith`, `toHaveReturnedWith` and similar matchers replace asymmetric matchers in their diffs.
- Multi-line `toAsymmetricMatcher()` output is indented when nested.

Note on labels: a failed `objectContaining`/`arrayContaining` is now printed without its label at any depth (`{` instead of `ObjectContaining {`), also in `error.expected`. Negated matchers keep their label: no value that passes them can be built, and their unchanged lines are the keys that caused the failure.

prs.title: fix(typecheck): kill the checker process tree on windows
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #9494

On Windows, tinyexec runs `tsc.cmd` through `cmd.exe`, so `Typechecker.stop()` only killed `cmd.exe`. The checker kept running and held the stdio pipes, so Vitest did not exit after watch mode closed. `stop()` now kills the whole tree with `taskkill /T /F`.

#11724 already fixed `vitest run` starting the checker in watch mode inside projects. This is the remaining part of the issue.

prs.title: fix: apply --shard before the test run starts
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11778

`--shard` was applied inside the pool, so the rest of the run (`onTestRunStart`, `onTestRunEnd`, coverage, global setup, the results cache) received the specifications of every shard. With `experimental.preParse`, the files of other shards had a parsed module that stayed `pending`, so the run failed.

Sharding is now the last selection step in `start()` and `collect()`, after the `preParse` filter. The parsed modules of other shards are not registered in the state. The pool only runs what it receives: the sequencer belongs to `Vitest`, and sorting moved out of the pool as well.

`runTestSpecifications` and `collectTests` no longer apply `--shard`, they run the specifications they receive (documented).

Also fixed:

- `vitest list --shard` ignored the shard with the default static parse and with `--filesOnly`
- with `preParse`, every file was registered twice in the state because `meta.typecheck` was `false` in the parsed file and missing in the collected one; files are now matched by `id`
- `TestModule.state()` never returned `queued` because it checked `result.state` instead of `mode`; a run with a `queued` module now fails like one with a `pending` module

prs.title: refactor: resolve browser trace locations in test run
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11753

Yet another follow-up TODO cleanup. The location mappings of the browser traceView artifact and the node traceTimeline artifact have divergent logic. This PR consolidates them to be processed in the same place.

prs.title: fix(ast-collect): only collect calls with a name argument
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #7432

Static collection treated any call on `test`/`describe` as a test, so method calls on a shadowed variable (`test.run({})`, `test.run(getValue())`) produced phantom tests. A call is now collected only if its first argument looks like a name: a string, template, number, identifier, member expression (`MyClass.name`), or a condition, `??`/`||` fallback or `+` concatenation of those. Custom methods like `test.fuzz('name', fn)` are still collected without config.

`test(getName(), fn)` is no longer collected.

prs.title: feat(cache): add a manifest to the fs module cache
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
`server.debug.dump` and `server.debug.load` stopped working when the fs module cache replaced the dump code (#9026): `dump` only wrote a metadata file, and nothing read `load`. Both options are deprecated and do nothing now.

Instead, Vitest writes `_manifest-<project>-<hash>.json` next to the fs module cache. It maps each module URL to its cache file, so the transformed code can be inspected or edited there.
